Manipulate nearest neighbor graphs

Source: R/knn-utils.R
knn-utilities.Rd

Truncate or reorder the neighbors in a graph, or adjust self neighbors in a graph of a dataset against itself. Each function returns a list containing only idx and dist matrices.

Usage

truncate_knn(graph, k)

sort_knn(graph, by = NULL)

remove_self_knn(graph, k = max(0L, ncol(graph$idx) - 1L))

self_first_knn(graph, k = ncol(graph$idx), self_dist = NULL)

Arguments

graph

A nearest neighbor graph with idx and dist matrices, such as the result of brute_force_knn().

k

Number of columns to retain. For truncate_knn(), from zero to the stored width. For remove_self_knn(), it is the number of nonself neighbors. For self_first_knn(), it is the total width including self, at least one. Supplying self_dist permits a width one greater than the stored width when every row has enough nonself neighbors.

by

Optional numeric matrix of scores with the same dimensions as the graph matrices. Defaults to the stored distances.

self_dist

Finite numeric scalar used when a row has no self entry. The default NULL errors if self is absent.

Value

A list containing the resulting idx and dist matrices.

Details

truncate_knn() keeps the first k columns. sort_knn() orders each row by ascending distance, or by the supplied score matrix. Ties retain their original order. Missing scores follow other scores, and missing neighbors (idx = 0) always come last. Distances remain paired with their indices.

remove_self_knn() keeps the first k present, nonself neighbors in each row (by default, one fewer than the stored width, with a minimum of zero). self_first_knn() puts self first, retaining the distance of the first existing self entry, and follows it with the first k - 1 present, nonself neighbors. If self is absent, supply self_dist to insert it. Both functions identify self by the row number, skip missing entries and other self entries, and error if a row has too few nonself neighbors. They are for self graphs. Do not use them on query results, where row numbers identify queries rather than reference observations.

Examples

graph <- brute_force_knn(iris[1:8, 1:4], k = 6)
truncate_knn(graph, k = 3)
#> $idx
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    1    5    8
#> [2,]    2    3    4
#> [3,]    3    4    7
#> [4,]    4    3    2
#> [5,]    5    1    8
#> [6,]    6    5    1
#> [7,]    7    3    4
#> [8,]    8    1    5
#> 
#> $dist
#>      [,1]      [,2]      [,3]
#> [1,]    0 0.1414212 0.1732050
#> [2,]    0 0.3000002 0.3316626
#> [3,]    0 0.2449490 0.2645751
#> [4,]    0 0.2449490 0.3316626
#> [5,]    0 0.1414212 0.2236066
#> [6,]    0 0.6164416 0.6164416
#> [7,]    0 0.2645751 0.3316627
#> [8,]    0 0.1732050 0.2236066
#> 
remove_self_knn(graph, k = 5)
#> $idx
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5]

#> [7,]    3    4    8    5    2

#> 
#> $dist
#>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3]      [,4]      [,5]
#> [1,] 0.1414212 0.1732050 0.5099020 0.5196152 0.5385164
#> [2,] 0.3000002 0.3316626 0.4242641 0.5099021 0.5385164
#> [3,] 0.2449490 0.2645751 0.3000002 0.4123107 0.5099019

#> [8,] 0.1732050 0.2236066 0.4123107 0.4242641 0.4242642
#> 
sort_knn(graph)
#> $idx
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]

#> [2,]    2    3    4    8    7    1
